## ARGENTINA — profile (page 124)

- **Header facts:** Region: Latin America & the Caribbean; Income group: Upper-middle-income; Lending category: IBRD; Data status: Data as reported (A); Population: 45.9 million; GNI: 669,197; Unit line: US$ million, unless otherwise indicated.
- **Total external debt stock, 2025:** 261,653, **+16.1% from 2024**.

- **Figure 1. Total external debt, 2015–25:**  
  Printed start/end values are **162,727** (2015) and **261,653** (2025). The line rises slightly at first, then climbs sharply to a peak/plateau around **≈2020–2021**, declines through **≈2022–2023**, edges up **≈2024**, dips slightly, and then rises strongly to **2025**, which appears to be the highest point.

- **Figure 2. External debt by creditor and creditor type in 2025, including IMF credit and SDR allocations:**  
  - **Total external debt:** 261,653
    - **Public & publicly guaranteed:** 180,489
    - **Private nonguaranteed:** 49,532
    - **Short-term:** 31,632
  - **Public & publicly guaranteed — by creditor type:** 180,489
    - **Multilateral:** 103,081
    - **Private creditors:** 73,172
    - **Bilateral:** 4,237
  - **Multilateral:** 103,081
    - **IMF credit:** 57,230
    - **IDB:** 19,300
    - **Other multilateral:** 26,551
  - **Bilateral:** 4,237
    - **China:** 3,084
    - **Germany:** 314
    - **Other bilateral:** 838

- **Figure 3. Debt ratios, 2015–25:**  
  - **External debt / exports:** **234%**, **+7.2%**. Line rises to a high around **≈2020**, then falls, partially rebounds, and ends near-flat to slightly up by 2025.  
  - **External debt / GNI:** **39%**, **+8.5%**. Line climbs steadily to a peak around **≈2021–2022**, drops sharply, then levels off with a slight uptick by 2025.  
  - **Debt service / exports:** **30%**, **-21.8%**. Line rises early to a high around **≈2018–2020**, declines, spikes again around **≈2023**, then falls to 2025.  
  - **Debt service / GNI:** **5%**, **-20.8%**. Line rises to a peak around **≈2020**, declines, has a modest rebound around **≈2023–2024**, then falls again by 2025.

- **Figure 4. Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025:**  
  - **Official creditors:** Maturity **24 yrs**; Grace period **6 yrs**; Interest rate **5.9%**
  - **Private creditors:** Maturity **2 yrs**; Grace period **2 yrs**; Interest rate **3.6%**

- **Notes:** Figure 3 shaded band shows the 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries.
- **Source:** World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.
